question: Should OpenClaw publicly support queryInstructionTemplate as an opt-in memory-search and plugin-provider contract for known model-id templates?
rationale: The model behavior is justified, but adding a config key and exported plugin SDK function establishes a compatibility-sensitive product contract that code review cannot approve implicitly.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Public Opt-In
options.body: Keep the default false, rebase onto the current shared embedding factory, document the stable contract, and prove both enabled and disabled upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep Preprocessing Provider-Internal
options.body: Implement the templates inside the owning OpenAI-compatible provider seam without adding a general public config or SDK helper.

options.title: Decline Built-In Templates
options.body: Leave query formatting to embedding servers or external plugins and close this PR after documenting the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow Public Opt-In
recommendation.body: Keep the default false, rebase onto the current shared embedding factory, document the stable contract, and prove both enabled and disabled upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history owns the central memory embedding and provider-boundary design affected by this public contract decision.
